fingerprint.fps: variable, 30 nominal; 12978 video frames in 662.50 s

interventions.what: Bandicam window capture of the Isle Wars Pro game window; the owner played one game from the options screen to the end screen (11:02 recording). The video file is the only output. No scripted clicks. Counters, seats and screens were read from pixels by region comparison and template matching of glyph shapes, with no OCR pass.

start_state.restore: Owner launched a new game on the unregistered Pro build from the options screen (seat 1 human, three computer seats, middle strength). Pro has no save file (C-SET-05), so no state was restored. The recording starts on the title screen; the opening deal is the first board.

args: probe: 662.50 s, 12978 video frames, variable frame rate (nominal 30), 1920x1080 H.264, AAC 48 kHz stereo, 87585120 bytes
ffmpeg 8.0.1; the panel regions were read frame by frame from the container timestamps; offsets are mm:ss.mmm video offsets
record content: the 87 attacks of the game (13 human, 74 computer; the last is inside the play-out and not resolved) with their start counters, strip states, endings and capture splits

observations.field: reading method
observations.value: the two-line counter strip (bottom right, "attacker armies against defender armies") was read at every frame where it changed, by matching glyph shapes of the digits (no OCR); the two country counters on the map were read before and after each attack by matching the large digits at the 46 country anchors; the owner of a country was read from its colour at the anchor (a selection or capture flash changes the colour for about 0.4 s, so owners right after a capture were not trusted and the counts decide). A capture is the country changing hands with the two counters adding up to the attacker armies at the capture; the last exchange of a capture is inferred (defender 1 to 0).

observations.field: what the strip shows first (a correction to how attack starts are read)
observations.value: For the human, the strip first shows the counters before any exchange (the map counters just before agree in all 13 cases). For the computer, in 46 of 73 attacks the map counters just before the strip appears are one exchange ahead of the strip's first state (the strip first appears after the first exchange): the start is taken from the map counters just before the strip (the "before" column), not from the strip's first state. Attacks whose before-counters were unreadable or unstable (30, 50, 71, 76, 86, 87) use the strip's first state and are marked.
